h1: Oakwood Residence Thonglor — full-kitchen apartments that feel like home in the heart of Bangkok's most fashionable district
intro: If you need more than just a room — space to unpack properly, a real kitchen to cook in and a washing machine without leaving the building — Oakwood Residence Sukhumvit Thonglor Bangkok is built exactly for that. Sixty-seven serviced apartment units run from a 46 sqm studio to a three-bedroom residence of 183 sqm, all with fully equipped kitchens, in-unit laundry and a complimentary shuttle to BTS Thong Lo. Set down the quiet lane of Soi Thonglor 13 within Sukhumvit 55, it places you right inside Thong Lo — one of Bangkok's most rewarding neighbourhoods for food, cafés and nightlife. Rates start from approx. THB 3,200/night, with a score of 8.5 from 608 verified reviews.

body.html: What separates Oakwood Residence Thonglor from a standard hotel is immediately clear: scale and self-sufficiency. Even the smallest studio starts at 46 sqm and arrives with a fully equipped kitchen, washer/dryer, dining table, proper desk and a sitting area separate from the bed. Step up to one-, two- or three-bedroom units and the space becomes genuinely apartment-like — something that families travelling with children, business travellers on extended assignments and groups of friends tend to find transformative after a few days.

Reviews consistently highlight the high cleanliness standards — a 9.2 cleanliness score across platforms sits noticeably above the district average. Housekeeping is praised for being thorough and unobtrusive, and reception staff come up repeatedly as friendly and willing to help. The most-mentioned practical perk, by some margin, is the complimentary shuttle service to BTS Thong Lo. The station is roughly a 15-minute walk in Bangkok's heat, so having a free tuk-tuk or car on hand changes the tone of the stay considerably.
"The room was enormous, the kitchen was genuinely usable, the washing machine saved us a fortune, and the staff couldn't have been friendlier — the shuttle to the BTS made everything easy."

Shared facilities are well maintained. The outdoor pool and modern gym are in good condition; the Residents' Lounge works equally well for a quiet evening in or an informal meeting; the children's play area is small but genuinely appreciated by guests with young kids. The two-level underground car park, provided free to all guests, is singled out by drivers as a rare commodity in a neighbourhood where street parking is nearly impossible.

The location in Soi Thonglor 13 is quieter than the main road, which most guests see as a plus. Step out onto Sukhumvit 55 and you are immediately in reach of the restaurants, cafés, supermarkets and community malls that define Thong Lo's appeal — from cheap noodle stalls to high-end Japanese omakase, from artisan coffee shops to the flagship club nights that draw Bangkok's after-dark crowd. For anywhere else in the city, the shuttle connects you to the BTS and the network from there is straightforward.

Honest accounts from real reviews surface a few consistent frustrations. Towels and pool towels draw repeated criticism for looking worn and outdated — an odd gap at a 4-star level that guests notice alongside otherwise well-kept facilities. Breakfast earns mixed marks: several reviewers cite a limited selection, poor-quality coffee and fruit that wasn't fresh. There are also occasional reports of a dismissive check-in experience, though this appears to reflect individual staff rather than policy.

Weighed up, Oakwood Residence Thonglor is a strong choice for anyone who genuinely needs apartment-style space in Thong Lo — and a less obvious fit for the traveller who wants a hotel experience with round-the-clock service polished to luxury standards. From around THB 3,200/night for a Studio Deluxe, the value against the square meterage is hard to argue with; the linens and the breakfast buffet are simply two areas the property hasn't kept pace with the rest of what it offers.

honestSummary: Oakwood Residence Thonglor is at its best for guests who genuinely want apartment-scale space and the convenience of a full kitchen in the Thong Lo district — families, long-stay business travellers and groups will find it close to ideal. The caveats are real: worn linens and a patchy breakfast buffet are recurring niggles that feel out of place at this price tier.
honestChecks: If you're a solo traveller staying one night and want a hotel seconds from the BTS — this property is a 15-minute walk from BTS Thong Lo and the shuttle runs on a schedule → boutique hotels nearer the station are a better fit for a quick overnight.

If linen and towel quality matters to you — multiple reviews flag worn, dated towels as a consistent sore point → if crisp 4-star bedding is non-negotiable, manage expectations or ask front desk on arrival.

If you're counting on a quality hotel breakfast each morning — the buffet receives genuinely mixed reviews on variety, coffee and fruit freshness → Thong Lo has outstanding breakfast cafés within walking distance that will outperform it easily.

tips.title: Make full use of the free shuttle
tips.body: The complimentary shuttle runs between the property and BTS Thong Lo — ask the front desk for the timetable on arrival. In Bangkok's heat, this saves the 15-minute walk and costs nothing.

tips.title: Cook in — the kitchen is genuinely equipped
tips.body: There's a supermarket within easy reach of the property. The kitchen has everything you need; for a week-long stay, cooking even a few meals in significantly cuts your food bill.

tips.title: Families: go for the Two-Bedroom
tips.body: The 2BR units at 117–134 sqm have separate sleeping areas, in-unit laundry and access to the children's play area — guests with young children say it made the whole trip far less stressful than a standard hotel room.

tips.title: Explore Thong Lo on foot in the evening
tips.body: Soi Thonglor 13 opens onto a neighbourhood full of restaurants, bars and coffee shops. Head out after sunset when the heat drops and the area comes alive — everything from street noodles to Japanese fine dining is within range.

faqTitle: FAQ — Oakwood Residence Sukhumvit Thonglor Bangkok

faq.q: Where is Oakwood Residence Thonglor and how do I get to BTS Thong Lo?
faq.a: The property is at 113 Soi Thonglor 13, Sukhumvit 55, Watthana district, Bangkok 10110. BTS Thong Lo is about a 15-minute walk away, but the hotel runs a complimentary shuttle to and from the station — ask the front desk for the timetable on arrival. From BTS Thong Lo you can reach Siam, Asok or Phrom Phong in just a few stops.

faq.q: What are the room types and starting prices at Oakwood Residence Thonglor?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 3,200/night for a Studio Deluxe (46–53 sqm with a full kitchen and washer/dryer), rising to Studio Premier, One Bedroom Premier (76–88 sqm), Two Bedroom Deluxe (117–134 sqm) and Three Bedroom units up to 183 sqm. Prices vary by dates and booking channel, so compare a few platforms before committing.

faq.q: Who is Oakwood Residence Thonglor best suited for?
faq.a: It suits families with children, business travellers on extended stays and groups of friends sharing a larger unit best. Anyone who wants to cook their own meals, do laundry in the room and spread out comfortably will feel at home here. It is less ideal for solo travellers on a one-night stay who need a hotel right on the BTS.

faq.q: Is there a pool and gym, and what are they like?
faq.a: Yes — an outdoor swimming pool, a modern fitness centre and a children's play area are all on-site and consistently praised in reviews for their cleanliness and condition. There is also a two-level underground car park provided free to all guests, which reviewers note is genuinely rare in Thong Lo.

faq.q: How is the breakfast at Oakwood Residence Thonglor?
faq.a: Reviews are mixed on breakfast — some guests are satisfied, but recurring criticisms mention a limited selection, poor-quality coffee and fruit that wasn't fresh. If a good breakfast matters to you, Thong Lo's café scene (within walking or shuttle distance) offers far better options for a similar or lower cost.

faq.q: Are the towels and room amenities up to a 4-star standard?
faq.a: This is a consistent weak point in the reviews. Towels and pool towels are frequently described as worn and dated, which reviewers feel is at odds with the otherwise well-maintained property. Everything else — the kitchen, furniture, cleanliness and facilities — draws positive comments; the linen quality is the area that needs attention.
